notes.title: Update of Those Who Came: Healing Solarus !!
notes.content:
Hello Gamers!

We have been able to check the Those Who Came status, and gather some of the issues that might have been affecting you all on your journey through Solarus. From the different issues found and also notified by you, we have been able to address most of them!

We have identified a critical issue that could cause the game to get stuck and force the players to restart the mission, forcing them to go through an unnecessary set of menus and maps.

There was a mission that could be blocked if the players skipped a step by opening a door before being asked, now the mission will keep going if the case is matched.

In addition to this major fix, we have been able to identify a set of more quality of life improvements and issues that were affecting the experience:

[list]
[*] Language typos mostly happening in Spanish and Catalan
[*] At the start of a mission, an empty dialogue box could appear and never fade
[*] Certain trees have been relocated and now they are not floating
[*] Modified map boundaries to properly adjust to the playable pathing
[*] Visual issue with certain consoles when using the Surface Walker suit
[*] Visual issue with the energy tubes that they weren’t displayed at the right pace, but all of them at the end of the quest
[*] Visual issue where certain objects where being occluded and were hardly visible
[*] Improved the visuals for the healing plants to make it easier to see when is healing
[*] Adjusted the Torek archives and the batteries to only appear when not obtained 
[/list]


We hope that with these fixes your experience with Those Who Came: Healing Solarus improves and helps you to reach Bineok. We need to save this world!

notes.title: Party time! A guide
notes.content:
Social Guide
How to add friends, send invites and join parties!

Having trouble setting up a party with your friends to join you on your journey through Solarus? Do not fret! This helpful guide should make your quest easier for you to focus on your mission.

How to send a friend request and set up a party
First of all, you should know that you have access to your “social menu” by opening up the “main menu” and going to the “social tab”, alternatively you can press [O] on your keyboard (or the left directional analog button on your gamepad) for quick access.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/8a7a5ec094872d236d0ca9e19ba83d145b14172b.png[/img]

Once you are on your “social menu”, on your left you should be able to see the option to add a player by name, be sure to type the exact username as the player that you want to add to your friendlist. Once you finished typing, press the [Add Friend] button below the search bar, that will send them an invite. If they correctly received an invitation from your end you’ll see a confirmation message on the bottom left corner of the menu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/6f2cdaa4fc35f5549590ad1d72e05a6e79b73714.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/41008e45d1d04dc88090d0c1546af5f0adbecc4e.png[/img]

If they accepted the invitation, you should be able to see them on your friend list, located at the right side of the social menu. Here you can also see which one of your friends is currently online. To send them an invitation to join your party you need to click on the icon located on the right side of their name.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/babef3b4361cf4170962f8b70cd0da9f9cbb1b1f.png[/img]

If they accept your invitation, they'll join your party. A notification will pop up on the top left corner of your screen anytime someone joins your party. You can see the members of your party on the left side of the social menu. From there you can also kick party members out of your group by pressing the kick button. Bye, friends!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/83e1cd684a7071b2219b03234179c071f7c9a1f6.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/8d7c03461a33be615c69105dce0152f6d718eda8.png[/img]

How to accept a friend request

Go to your social menu to see if you’ve received any friend requests. On the right side of the social menu you should be able to see all of your pending friend requests. The two icons located right next to their name are the options to accept or to reject a request. If you accept the request they’ll be added to your friend list.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/9c9622e33589b3ea004304f2daae14deb94bac35.png[/img]

How to accept a party invite

A notification will pop up from the top of your screen if you’ve received a party invite. You’ll have the option to accept or to reject. If you accept the invitation you’ll join their party as a member and will be able to join the same adventures as your friends!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/55bf8bd6352fde34eef3537af52dcdf59e1831b4.png[/img]


Remember you can always join our Discord Channel in case you have any doubts and suggestions on how to polish our products 100% !

Happy gaming!

notes.title: Solaru’s Inhabitants: The Torek
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/d79249ac21e00818648a89c0bb5a2d0d20bef6e3.jpg[/img]


Hello again fellow explorers, here we are with another chapter of your training as a Sainen pioneer amidst the thrilling lands of Solarus. In today’s masterclass we are going to discuss the nature of Solarus' fellow inhabitants, the Torek. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/fc3e17be8bdde91fc280771d8ab6faf6c6c4119a.png[/img]

The Torek are descendants of what humans call “Lizards”, a common creature in the Universe. In this case though, they have evolved until they became a civilization type I in Kardashev’s Scale. They are a bit more advanced than our human neighbors, but a lot less than us, the Sainen. We belong to type III!

All Torek look very similar to each other, and while there is not much difference between them, they have completely different attitudes towards us! Let’s see:


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/f3eea8dc359f75526fc09207000bed97207aa182.gif[/img]


[b]Friendly Torek[/b]

You may bump into them from time to time. They sport a friendly attitude because deep down they know you come in peace and want to restore life in their home planet. As a consequence, they will try to bring you aid in the form of goods or information. Kolra, an important character among the Torek, or Commander Toan, in charge of Torek’s operations, fall into this category and will accompany you in your journey.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/441141e53636dbdb95b324015f461197386741f1.gif[/img]


[b]Vendors [/b]

They are inherently good and will exchange money or resources with you. In future versions of Those Who Came, they will be key for your missions since they have valuable information about the new planet you are exploring. You will be able to obtain new suits, technology or important items in your missions thanks to their help.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/1e57481ed3a09e97893de5ff52ee6e4c3eceb9b1.gif[/img]


[b]The Guardians of Solarus[/b]

These Torek have seen the worst in their homeland while being in touch with the corruption ravaging planet Solarus. As a result, they have suffered a lot and won’t hesitate attacking you when they consider you’ve approached an object, structure or important element they are guarding. They look at Sainen as another potential threat that could destroy them. 

This group of Toreks are broad and some of them will throw different attacks towards you. Even though their attacks are usually defensive or indirect and will just sabotage your purpose, here are some hints to get your crew prepared:

[list]
[*] [b]Area Guarding[/b]
The Torek will create a round area in front of them. If they catch you inside this area your Suit Shield will get damaged and your life will be compromised! Please, check your life bar placed in the lower left corner of your screen if you are caught in this situation. 

[*] [b]Dart Guarding[/b]
Some Torek have a bracelet equipped with darts that provoke our movements to be half time slower than originally, it would seem you had consumed one of those human beverages drunk at parties on Earth. We know you would not! Just avoid this situation, explorer!

[*] [b]Trap Guarding[/b]
Just beside the Dart Guardians, there are some Torek that like to persecute and catch you in their arms. They don’t want to kill you, they just try to avoid you entering places “you shouldn’t be in” by propelling you outside that zone once they’ve put their broad hands all over. 
[/list]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/b8071e37032cd3e1eda341580804e20af0af0ac6.gif[/img]


As you can see, Torek come in all forms and sizes, but their key to know what’s their deal is actually paying attention to their actions! 

Which of these Torek guarding techniques will be more challenging to you? Tell us in the comment section, or [url=https://discord.com/invite/c8ZXujGhN7]join our Discord community[/url] today.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/7c2e73b9eb046815d27c28631cc2a6f26647ec2d.png[/img]

Happy gaming!

notes.title: Dressed to Survive!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/ccfe04be97b72acb5a0cd35d2e45f011dc53a0dc.jpg[/img]


Greetings, fellow explorers! 
You may have noticed; you are exploring Solarus with your crew and suddenly one of your teammates collapses after walking on boiling lava, or doesn't mind their step and falls into a rocky pit, or is smashed under the arms of an angry Torek. Either way, your poor colleague may be a bit low on life. Do not worry. There is a small piece of technology that will revive the most smashed of Sainen Explorers. And that piece is so easy to put on it’s even called E.C.A Suit. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/38dfecea21e8004a3dd7017d08c018b6021e62c0.jpg[/img]

But what does E.C.A stand for?

These letters mean: Experimental Connectivity Attire, an experimental suit especially designed to use your surroundings for your own benefit, easing survival amidst the inclement outdoors of Solarus. Its technology allows harvesting wild plants not available in normal conditions. 

After the Energy of these plants is processed, the E.C.A Suit will be ready for you to use the 
"Pulse Emitter", a skill bound to the suit that will transfer Vital Energy to nearby teammates. Just remember to click on your “R” button to rescue your crew. And right in the spot where they fell firsthand, they will be up and running lively in no time!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/fe0a18c573e54bd967d03237f0fc2caba6e23e14.gif[/img]

Where can you get the E.C.A Suit?

On Surface Expeditions watch out for a mission especially led to investigate a branch of exotic alien plants. Your purpose is to gather all information possible about the flora and bring the results of this investigation to Dr. Welsen. The almighty doctor will then talk to you and craft the E.C.A Suit for you. 

Now you are ready to easen up your missions at Solarus! Remember to craft all the goods you need, or purchase them in our Colonial Market, serving your sensitive Sainen’s skin from Solarus and beyond.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/e293815ca9289c4724e7c8bcbdabab9a726457f8.gif[/img]

notes.title: Dressed to Hack!

Hell-oh, fellow explorers! 

Have you noticed how fast February is approaching its end? We hope you are well rested and gathering all your energy for diving into our next news. Some weeks ago in this post(link) we told you about the marvelous perks of having a well crafted wardrobe in Those Who Came. Now it is time to introduce you to one of the most important suits early in the game and one that will amaze the techiest of friends among your crew: The Technician Suit.

[b]Perks of dressing with the Technician Suit[/b]
This suit translates Torek’s technology into Sainen’s. In doing so, the technician is able to hack the Terminal and modify its original behaviour. This unlocks certain parts of the planet when completing missions gradually. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/1a8a2de8d0d6ff140038a8c06025da2d00c4b698.gif[/img]

For example, a Sainen with Jointer Energy can empower one of the said Torek Terminals, but only if the Sainen is dressed up with the almighty Technician suit then they can interact with the Terminal itself. 

Watch out! There are different types of Torek Technology Terminals that may be needed to interact with, like types of doors, structures or a particular type of generator. Play as you wish! And be technical about it ːsteamhappyː

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/f9dd87d99c095f6cf3965337c33575f6edeace08.gif[/img]

[b]Where can it be found?[/b]
First, it is crucial to be in “Solarus Expedition”. Once there, look for a Gearing Pod available on the surface. Put on your first dress: the Explorer Base Suit. Solarus doesn’t need to look at your undergarments. Complete the mission with your crew. Once you’ve survived, go to Dr. Welsen and request the Technician suit. He needs some materials that can be found on the surface. Do not worry, if you have looked for them well enough, he will be able to craft this shiny and new suit for you. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/fd8a7856495b9f195711c60a9eb8e974528199ff.gif[/img]

notes.title: The Stadium, a PvP Guide.
notes.content:

This is why Sainen’s top pioneers have access to [b]The Stadium[/b], an area in which they can compete against each other by building two teams. The objective? Storing a huge amount of super valuable energy in your team’s battery before your competitors fill in theirs. [b]The crew members that have stored the most energy win the match![/b] 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/12373ed281287dd83c8bfc8b1e7b69fdd6b0c13e.gif[/img]


Of course, this comes with some fun challenges, like preventing your counterparts from gathering energy, preparing obstacles and overall sabotaging their objective in a hilarious manner, the Sainen style. As we detailed in our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1708570/view/3106919419853170312]previous blog post[/url], the Sainen are defined by their amazing ability to adapt to difficulties and continue to produce great technical and scientific innovations even under adverse circumstances. This is how they managed to become a type III civilization in the Kardashev scale. Today we're back on our dev blog to tell you a bit more about one of their greatest inventions: the [b]Explorer Suit[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/2713ee8b06cfdb70ae773532c08dbab1a0c5c7ac.png[/img]

This piece of clothing [b]protects the Sainen's body from getting hurt by extreme temperatures[/b] and contains several slots that improve its performance with special skills – try them in the game by pressing [R]! By using the modern technology of shapers, these suits also work as [b]portable batteries[/b] where the Sainen explorers store energy for later use.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/08812880d763d13e6f8376c732d425ce1a54deaa.png[/img]

You’ll have to unlock them all to successfully complete the most complicated missions of Those Who Came. Regarding the enhancers already mentioned, you’ll unlock them through the online store located in your personal ship, or by crafting it from raw materials at your workshop.

There are four types of suits available in the game, and the [b]Explorer Base Suit[/b] is the simplest of all them. Later, the [b]Agile Explorer Suit[/b] will allow you to walk and run faster, your power reserve will increase with the [b]Energy Explorer Suit[/b], and the [b]Heavy Explorer Suit[/b] will make you stronger. As we explained in our previous post, each one of these tools will focus you on a cooperation and survival strategy different from the others.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/3f487166853393aa7e53b8f5c36a3cd01a810989.png[/img]

Said that, we can’t wait to discover which one is your favorite. Tell us in the comment section, or [url=https://discord.com/invite/c8ZXujGhN7]join our Discord community[/url] today.

See you in the next post!

notes.title: The origin and binding of energies
notes.content:
A fundamental law of physics says that energy is never created out of nothing, nor can it be destroyed, it just takes on another form. It works not just on Earth, but for any phenomenon within our observable universe. [b]Stars, nebulae, black holes... are pure energy.[/b] Even though we cannot perceive it with our current technology, those regions that seem empty and desolate seem to be full of what we call "dark matter". The passage of millennia only changes its distribution, but never the amount of existing energy.

Since the Sainen cannot use these energies on their own, they spent several decades perfecting [b]a technology that allowed them to channel this powerful resource[/b]. Such a relevant invention as the shapers meant a great scientific breakthrough for the species, and also positioned the species as a [b]type III civilization[/b] in the Kardashev scale. A good example of how they use energy are the elemental abilities they mastered for exploration and scouting missions, as the one they’re carrying out in Solarus to avoid a new cataclysm.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/3accbc8eb18305c85fd95f71d4dedac11853bf43.png[/img]

[b]Firei, Airy, Jointer, Ether.[b] These names will be familiar to you if you've frequented our Twitter and Instagram accounts. Each of these energies will mean [b]a different strategy to survive[/b] the growing aggressiveness of Solarus. They will allow the Sainen to interact with the environment by flying over obstacles, passing through solid bodies, activating electronic devices and much more. Of course, all the energy in the universe cannot be summed up in those four types — there are many more to be discovered!

The use of shapers doesn’t mean that all energies are easy to master. It depends on the type, and on the [b]affinity[/b] that a Sainen has with each of them. The stronger their connection is, the easier it will be for the subject to master that energy. However, there will be those who aim to perfectly [b]master all four types[/b], but the preparation training is so hard that few manage to overcome it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/0dac4e61de9e86f0436ef5c602427dc488c36dff.gif[/img]

As you progress in the exploration of Solarus and find blueprints for enhanced suits, you will discover new ways to use energies. But the true key to success in each mission of Those Who Came is to [b]work as a team combining the use of these energies[/b]. After all, the Sainen are a collaborative civilization. For them, the pursuit of a common goal outweighs any differences, and you can also feel it in their relationship with the Torek.

Is there any other aspect of the energies you would like to learn about? Let us know in the comment section below or join the discussion in our [url=https://discord.com/invite/aSNuvRsUHj]Discord server[/url] — we’ll be happy to find you there!

notes.title: X-MASS update coming on December 9th
notes.content:
Morning, explorers,

As we told you on Twitter last Friday, we are very happy to announce that the next [b]major update[/b] for Those Who Came is about to be released. 

The update will hit Steam [b]on December 9th[/b] with more content, technical improvements to the game's core features and much more. We truly believe this is a significant leap forward compared to previous builds, and one that puts us closer to our vision for Those Who Came. 

With this new update, we have made some changes to our [b]roadmap[/b], you can check them below.


⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/897d5fcd308117a21597f6152a386c4aca88971b.jpg[/img]

Among the new features, we have renamed some mechanics, and introduced some slight changes in the number of players that will be needed to complete some tasks. We have also tweaked the party system to create a more seamless experience, added new maps and did a ton of bug fixing.

Let's spell the changes out part by part!


[b][h3]Adapting the terminology[/h3][/b]
Science fiction transports players to futuristic contexts — often far removed from their own in both space and time — where scientific and technological innovations define everything. In contrast to fantasy works, here unlikely events must have a logical and rational basis. For this very reason, we understand that words like "magic", or “spells”, don’t fit a story like ours. Therefore, the upcoming patch will rename the elemental abilities of the Sainen: from now on, we’ll always refer to them as “Energies”.


⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/5cb4f3acc8fbff9042e5bb3136c5779b241e05a8.jpg[/img]

In this sci-fi context, the devices used by the Sainen to catalyze these energies of the Universe will be called “Shapers”, not “magic props”; and each player will be able to set four types of configuration depending on the ability we need to use.

Also, for the sake of consistency, the way in which the chosen shaper is configured will be called “configuration” instead of the previous “spell”.


[b][h3]Tweaked energies[/h3][/b]
The Sainen, as an advanced civilization, are capable of [b]handling special energies that serve them as a way to interact with the environment[/b] in many different ways. 

There are [b]4 different types of energies[/b], all related to a specific element:

[list]
[*] [b]Airy:[/b] Levitation. Creates energy flows that make the player ascend and be able to access unreachable areas. It also prevents them from big falls. 
[*] [b]Firei:[/b] Glowing Orb. The Firei energy becomes a light in the darkness, and can melt down certain objects. 
[*] [b]Ether:[/b] Shade. Ether gives the players the ability to reshape themselves or other objects. This is useful to go through walls and strong structures to reach new areas.
[*] [b]Jointer:[/b] Object transmutation. Jointer empowers your companions and creates new paths by energizing the environment.
[/list]

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/1733b23d6d48156cac39b3b4d72f61fa6bfae65e.jpg[/img]

In order to use the energies, each Sainen will first need to establish a link with the ability they want to master, and will have the option to practice in a tutorial level specifically designed for this purpose. Your kind has awakened after a long period of time, and will need to start all over again from scratch; thus, you will begin learning any ability from the basic level.

During your mission on planet Solarus, you will find some energy spikes to capture and get some “configurations”; that is, the way to set up the devices -”Shapers”- to generate the energies.


⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/36fcf0db775b2828d843dd7f49e88b73e98abe84.jpg[/img]

The energy skill levels range from 1 to 50, which is the highest. As you level up, using the energies will become increasingly difficult, even much more if you are trying to excel in all of them. Playing with friends means that each of your companions can specialize in one or two of these energies, depending on the number of players. However, it is also possible for only one player to master all of them -it’s extremely challenging, but achievable!


[b][h3]Multiplayer experience[/h3][/b]
Those Who Came is a [b]multiplayer game[/b]. We recommend that you gather [b]4 friends[/b] to be able to enjoy the whole experience, but there are several missions that can be played in Single player mode, and others that will require a minimum of 2 players. For the last missions you may need all the 4 to complete the adventure. We have tweaked this number as before there were some missions that needed up to 7 players to be completed.


⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/5f82743d02937d2774478b60f50ac7abc2a86efa.jpg[/img]

Remember that as a crew, you have access to a PvP area called The Stadium that can only be enjoyed in multiplayer mode. It is a very exciting place where you can upgrade your equipment, earn Halis, and test your skills with the energy you have gathered -not individually, but with your friends! PvP can be played in two groups of 2, the minimum required, two groups of 3, or two groups of 4. There are several options for two different parties to play together, and have fun while mastering their energies!


⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/fad235802b2095c44034bd0ac227a6aae4fa62bd.jpg[/img]


[b][h3]New maps[/h3][/b]
Along their journey, the Sainen will have to learn about Solarus, the planet that is meant to be their new home: its surface, its environment, its fauna and flora, and how to establish contact with the natives. Solarus also changes its behaviour depending on the day and night cycles! 

The next update will bring some very interesting new areas to the map. For example, the Torek’s Cave, an unknown part of the planet with some environmental peculiarities, where the native inhabitants of the planet, the Torek, are surprisingly able to live. The Sainen will need to discover Solarus and its possibilities through the different missions; it’s a vast planet with many areas to explore, so it won’t be an easy task!


⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/ca1e641d601c313e46cf744d4982b403831f2d7f.jpg[/img]

All these new places will help the Sainen to understand more about Solarus' history, and discover relevant elements that will have a key impact on how to heal the planet and make it fit to live in. 


[b][h3]Characters[/h3][/b]
The update of Dec 9th will also bring [b]new names to certain elements and characters in the story[/b]. We have been thinking on how some of them could be improved to better fit the story and the world we have created. With this in mind, we decided to rename some of them; the most remarkable changes are the name of the Sainen Commander, who we will call Artissa from now on, and the main ship, HERMAION.


⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41111472/4d73ab66d2f2e463ee0d0fd05e592734f7c74bee.jpg[/img]

Another important decision has been to [b]discard all characters’ voices[/b]. We realised that too many new recordings would be needed, as the number of NPCs with dialogues we had originally planned to include in the story had increased considerably. Instead, we will use very brief sounds to identify the speaker, and will most likely review sounds and voices thoroughly in upcoming updates. 


[b][h3]Bug fixing and QoL improvements[/h3][/b]
We have also added some hotfixes to this new update. Regarding our party system, for instance, we have solved several bugs in order to improve performance and stability, while including several quality of life improvements. Besides, as usual with a new update, we have polished the build to remove bugs. 




Here are all the things to [b]look forward to on Dec 9th[/b]! 

For more news, updates, or a friendly chat about the game, we invite you to follow and join the conversations here on the [b]Steam forums[/b], our community on [b][url=https://discord.com/invite/aSNuvRsUHj]Discord[/url][/b], and our social media channels, [b][url=https://mobile.twitter.com/rolldboxgames]Twitter[/url][/b], [b][url=https://www.instagram.com/rolldboxgames/]Instagram[/url][/b] and [b][url=https://www.reddit.com/user/rolldboxgames/]Reddit[/url][/b].

Take care and have a great week!

notes.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
notes.content:
Greetings, explorer. If this is your first time checking Those Who Came on Steam, surely you will have a lot of questions. Let’s get started to solve them all!

[b][u]GENERAL QUESTIONS[/u][/b]

[b]First of all, what kind of game is Those Who Came?[/b]
We define it as a sci-fi cooperative survival RPG. Players will follow the story of the Sainen, a strong and resilient species that nearly faced extinction after their planet collapsed. Hoping for their kind to survive this cataclysmic event, they sent forth a ship full of explorers frozen in a cryogenic state. You and your friends will become four young survivors called to explore a new planet: Solarus. The planet seems to be in danger, just as yours was, so it’s in the hands of your race, and your local allies, the healing of this land you expect to call “home” someday…

[b]What is the game about?[/b]
In each mission, you will explore a new area of Solarus in search of different ways to help the planet: from researching the local vegetation to restoring some destroyed energy facilities. Every action counts, so the most important factor to achieve success is planned cooperation: decide your individual roles as a team, and never leave the rest behind!  

[b]What requirements must my PC meet to run the game under the best conditions?[/b]
Our recommended system requirements are:
[list]
[*] OS: Windows 10
[*] Memory: 16 GB RAM
[*] Storage: 15 GB available space
[/list]
To play it under the minimum system requirements you just need:
[list]
[*] OS: Windows 10
[*] Memory: 8 GB RAM
[*] Storage: 15 GB available space
[/list]

[b]When did the development start?[/b]
By August 2020, the pandemic really awakened our game developer senses! We explored several ideas and this was the one we liked the most. 

[b]What else should I know about the development process?[/b]
Our main work tool was Unreal Engine 4 -- version 4.25.4. Plus, the game is developed with a mix of Blueprints (for environmental artists and game designers), and C++ (programmers). Most of our content is custom-made; we only use plugins to improve the connections to our servers and track data for game improvement.



[b][u]EARLY ACCESS & FULL GAME VERSIONS[/u][/b]

[b]Why Early Access?[/b]
When we set out to develop Those Who Came, we wanted to challenge some of the foundations of the RPG genre, like its emphasis on combat. We want to create a refreshing experience, something that feels new and unique. Testing and honing these ideas with real players will allow the game to grow to its true potential.

[b]How long will the game be in EA?[/b]
Our goal is to transition to full release during 2022 as soon as we feel the game is content-complete and polished, ensuring an engaging experience for all our players.

[b]How is the full version planned to differ from the EA version?[/b]
The full version is planned to include new maps, more creatures, extra suits, and new special powers. The feedback of the community will be a key factor not just to polish these features, but to set the priorities and decide their final shape.

[b]What is the current state of the EA version?[/b]
The core mechanics and features of the game are already implemented: you can create teams and add friends, craft and trade goods in cooperation with other players, explore the landing zone on Solarus, and compete at the Stadium in PvP. You can also use the 4 initial special powers, in combination with a varied set of suits and suit mods. We are working hard on balancing, as well as polishing the currently available maps. In terms of stability and performance, the game still has some bugs – but most of them are known and identified, and we are working to iron them out.

[b]Will the game be priced differently during and after EA?[/b]
The price will increase on full release as the game receives more content.

[b]Is the game coming to other platforms?[/b]
We’d love to ensure that there will be a console version, but Those Who Came is still in Early Access and our priority now is to make a game we can feel proud of.



[b][u]GAMEPLAY[/u][/b]

[b]What kind of missions can you play in Those Who Came?[/b]
Travel to different areas of Solarus to follow the storyline, or join the Arena to have fun competing against other Sainen explorers -- of course, in a friendly, non-combat way! Both game modes require more players to join forces with you, so these teammates will be chosen by the matchmaking system unless you invite your friends. And yes, that means that a stable internet connection is required to play Those Who Came.

[b]How does the Arena work?[/b]
Explore the map in search of charged generators to extract energy for your headquarters as you try to sabotage your enemy’s supply before you run out of time.

[b]Will you add more story chapters over the course of the Early Access period?[/b]
Yes. We’re still figuring out how to blend the narrative aspect of Those Who Came with its gameplay. It will take some time, but our plan consists in updating the game little by little with new missions, features, maps, and characters. Just wait and see!

[b]How many friends can I invite to join my party?[/b]
In Solarus, you’ll recruit three companions to complete the story missions. At the Arena, up to eight players will be able to join you as allies or rivals in 2v2, 3v3, and 4v4 “battles”.

[b]What do you do to protect players against toxic behaviors?[/b]
According to the essence of Those Who Came, we expect to minimize the possibility of getting exposed to toxic behaviors and build a comfortable space for all kinds of players. That’s the reason why we refused to include chat features. Players can interact by using animated emotes, and talk via third-party apps like Discord or Teamspeak.

[b]Are you planning a single-player mode?[/b]
Those Who Came reaches its full potential as a multiplayer game, given that we decided to focus on cooperation as the best way to save Solarus -- but yes, the single-player mode is in our roadmap!



[b][u]USER SUPPORT[/u][/b]

[b]Am I allowed to customize my keyboard shortcuts?[/b]
We’ll enable the option at some point in the Early Access phase.

[b]Will the game support controllers?[/b]
It will!

[b]Where can I report bugs?[/b]
In the game, press ESC to open the Home Menu and select the bug icon at the bottom right corner of the screen. It will take you to our official Support form, where you can send us a detailed explanation and attach a screenshot. Also, we usually read the discussions here on Steam, so feel free to share your issues. But if you need a quick response, we recommend you to join our official Discord server or contact us via Twitter -- our DMs are always open!

[b]How long do I have to wait before the issue is solved?[/b]
Our support team checks their inbox and the Discord server on a daily basis. Since not all bugs are of equal severity, we ask for your patience while we look for the best way to deal with each problem. If a bug significantly disrupts the gameplay experience, it will be given the highest priority and we will proceed to fix it immediately.

[b]Can I suggest new features too?[/b]
Of course! We’re always happy to read what players think about our work and how do they think it can be improved -- but please remember that we need a reasonable time to determine whether the suggested feature fits within our design and the objectives set for the game.
